blocks.text: 1. Query, Key, And Value

blocks.alt: A query compares against a key to produce a weighted value

blocks.text: Encoder-Decoder Attention, the previous topic, computed relevance scores by comparing decoder state against encoder outputs. Query, Key, and Value give a closer, more formal look at how relevance scores actually get computed.
This is the genuinely standard vocabulary and structure underlying every Attention mechanism covered in this module, explored in complete depth throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Comparison Being Formalized

This connects back to computing relevance scores, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention. Comparing the decoder's own state against every encoder position, already covered there, was described only generally in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely formalizes exactly what gets compared to what, replacing that earlier general description with genuinely precise, standard terminology.
3. The Query, Explained

blocks.alt: The current position produces a query asking what it is looking for

blocks.text: The genuinely first of three roles, the Query, connects back to the decoder's own current state, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention. It represents genuinely what the current step is looking for.
This gives a genuinely precise name to the decoder state's own role already covered generally in that earlier topic, the genuinely asking side of the comparison.

blocks.text: 4. The Key, Explained

blocks.alt: Each position produces a key describing what it offers

blocks.text: This connects back to every single encoder position, already covered in Why Attention. The genuinely second role, the Key, represents what each encoder position genuinely offers.
It is used specifically to genuinely compare against the Query, already covered in the previous section, the genuinely answering side of that same comparison.
5. The Value, Explained

blocks.alt: Each position produces a value holding what it actually contains

blocks.text: This connects back to the weighted sum computation, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention. The genuinely third role, the Value, is what genuinely actually gets summed together once attention weights are known.
This is the genuinely actual content contributed to the final context vector, a genuinely distinct role from the Key already covered in the previous section, explored further in the next section.
6. The Key Versus Value Distinction

blocks.alt: The key is used for matching while the value is used for content

blocks.text: A genuinely important, subtle distinction connects back to the Key and Value, both already covered in this topic. The Key is used genuinely for comparison; the Value is used genuinely for the actual content contributed.

This genuinely subtle but important separation, already covered in this section, lets a network genuinely learn different, specialized representations for "how to be found" versus "what to actually provide."

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This distinction, already covered in this topic, is genuinely subtle since the Key and Value often derive from the same underlying position, yet are genuinely learned as separate, specialized representations serving two different purposes.

blocks.text: 7. Learned Projections

blocks.alt: An input vector is projected by learned weight matrices into query and key

blocks.text: This connects back to filters being genuinely learned, already covered in Filters and Kernels. Query, Key, and Value genuinely each come from their own separate, learned linear transformation.
This holds rather than genuinely being raw, unprocessed encoder or decoder states directly, giving the network genuinely learned flexibility in how it represents each of these three distinct roles.
8. The Scoring Step, Precisely Connected
This connects back to computing relevance scores, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention. The Query genuinely gets compared against every Key to produce those genuinely relevance scores.
This is exactly the comparison already covered generally in that earlier topic, now precisely named using the Query and Key vocabulary already covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 9. Why This Framework Genuinely Generalizes

blocks.alt: Query, key, and value apply to self, cross, and multi-head attention

blocks.text: A genuinely important, forward-looking observation connects forward to Self-Attention, covered later in this module. This exact Query-Key-Value framework genuinely applies far beyond just Encoder-Decoder Attention alone.

This genuinely general applicability, already covered in this section, is exactly why this vocabulary, already covered throughout this topic, became the genuinely standard way of describing Attention across the entire field.
10. Recognizing Why This Vocabulary Is Genuinely Essential Going Forward
This connects back to every remaining topic throughout this entire module. Every single one genuinely uses this exact Query, Key, Value framework, already covered in this topic.
This connects forward to Transformers, covered later in this course, built almost entirely from this vocabulary. Understanding it now, already covered, is a genuinely necessary foundation.
11. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates computing Query, Key, and Value through separate learned projections, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 4
qkv_size = 4

decoder_state = rng.normal(size=hidden_size)
encoder_outputs = rng.normal(size=(5, hidden_size))

# already covered as learned projections in this topic
W_query = rng.normal(size=(qkv_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W_key = rng.normal(size=(qkv_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W_value = rng.normal(size=(qkv_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1

query = W_query @ decoder_state  # already covered as the Query in this topic
keys = np.array([W_key @ enc_out for enc_out in encoder_outputs])   # already covered as the Key in this topic
values = np.array([W_value @ enc_out for enc_out in encoder_outputs])  # already covered as the Value in this topic

print(f"Query shape: {query.shape}")
print(f"Keys shape: {keys.shape}")
print(f"Values shape: {values.shape}")
print("\nQuery, Key, and Value each came from their own genuinely separate, learned linear transformation, already covered in this topic")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the exact same encoder output producing genuinely different Key and Value representations, each from its own separate, learned projection, exactly the distinction already covered as this topic's own core insight.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Query, Key, and Value formalize how relevance scores actually get computed in Attention.
The Query represents what the current step is looking for.
The Key represents what each position offers, used for comparison against the Query.
The Value is what actually gets summed together once attention weights are known.
Key and Value serve genuinely different, specialized purposes: comparison versus content.
Query, Key, and Value each come from their own separate, learned linear transformation.
The Query compared against every Key produces the relevance scores.
This exact framework generalizes far beyond Encoder-Decoder Attention, becoming standard vocabulary.
Next up: Dot-Product Attention, the simplest concrete way to actually compute these relevance scores.
